Nothing was under review — there is no `docs/reviews/1-t-0019.md` and no finding, so nothing is upheld or overruled. What was actually disputed was whether T-0019 could proceed at all: its step 1 precondition PD2 (`account_settings_path` on `origin/main`) is false, it is still false today, and three sessions in a row correctly stopped on it and therefore pushed nothing, which the factory read as an unpushed failure each time. That reading is what I overrule: a card blocked on one clause of one row is not a blocked card. What now holds is the standing rule that a session finishes every part of the scope that is not blocked and names what it left out — so T-0019 lands as `b90601e` with the whole of §2.5's operator surface (`asf approvals`, `list`, `resolve`) and the doctor's `approvals` row on its three clauses that need nothing from Task 3, and A5 passes green at 15 tests. What changes because of it: PD2 is demoted from a stop to a scope boundary for this card — it no longer gates T-0019, only the one `for` loop that the fourth clause will be, and this finding never returns in a later round. T-0019's remaining dependency is F-0031 Task 3's alone, and it is recorded in the code where the loop will go rather than in a hold.
NEEDS OPERATOR: F-0031 Task 3 (`asf hooks install` puts the approvals hook in every worker account, plan `docs/plans/f-0031.md:193`) is the last thing between the doctor row and its fourth clause — confirm it is carded and sequenced, then have that card add the worker-account loop to `approvals.check_doctor`. Recommendation: let Task 3 own that loop, since it is the task that creates the entry the loop looks for.

The dispute was not a review finding — there is no docs/reviews/1-t-0020.md, and the branch carried nothing; three sessions in a row ended with worker/T-0020 at origin/main, and the feeder read each as an `unpushed` correction until the round cap. The cause is the plan's own PD2 guard: step 1 of Task 5 in docs/plans/f-0031.md tells the session to check `git show origin/main:asf/approvals.py | grep -q "def cmd_approvals"` and, failing it, to print NEEDS OPERATOR and end without writing code. I checked that anchor against the checkout: `cmd_approvals` is indeed absent from origin/main (asf/approvals.py there defines up to `_enforce` at line 438 and no CLI), so every one of those sessions obeyed the plan correctly — and obeying it is what the factory scores as failure, since a session that writes nothing has nothing to push. That is the stalemate, and no further correction round could have broken it. I overrule PD2's block for T-0020. PD2's stated rationale is that "a session built on a trunk without its base would re-invent it", and Task 5 re-invents nothing: its real base is `open_holds`, `holds`, `_fold`, `append` and `CLASSES` in asf/approvals.py (lines 38, 296, 329, 336, 256 on origin/main) and `job_name` in asf/tick/step_wave.py (line 116 on origin/main) — all on the trunk. The `cmd_approvals` grep is an ordering proxy for Task 4, not a dependency of anything Task 5 writes. What now holds: Task 5 is built and on the branch. `approvals.raise_holds(ctx, out)` raises one verbatim NEEDS OPERATOR line per open human-now hold oldest first, one summary line for groom holds, writes the `held`/`hold-resolved` events once each through the ledger's `announced`/`closed` markers, and answers `{item: (class, level)}`; `step_wave.run` calls it first and parks a held launching row with `waits <job> <item> — held <class> (<level>)` instead of briefing it. All four A3 methods of TickRaiseTest pass, the full suite is green at 1068, and this finding does not come back in a later round. What changes because of it: the footprint T-0020 shares with T-0019 (asf/approvals.py, tests/test_approvals.py) is now written by whichever lands first — my additions are appended at the end of both files precisely so a T-0019 rebase over them is mechanical, and the factory's CONFLICT → REBASE lane owns that, not another adjudication. PD2 itself stands for the Tasks where the grep names a symbol the Task actually calls (Task 4's `hooks.account_settings_path` is one); it should not be read as a wave-order assertion, and where it blocks, the session must still push the NEEDS OPERATOR finding rather than end empty — an empty branch is indistinguishable from a dead session and loops forever, which is exactly what happened here three times.
NEEDS OPERATOR: F-0031 Task 3 (T-0018) has no branch on origin, and Tasks 4 and 6 (worker/T-0019, worker/T-0021) sit empty at origin/main for the same PD2 reason — launch T-0018, land it, then relaunch T-0019 and T-0021.

Two things were disputed and neither survives. First, the plan's PD2 step-1 guard for Task 5 tells the session to grep origin/main for `def cmd_approvals` — T-0019's symbol, which nothing in Task 5 reads — and three sessions read that literally and stopped; that finding is OVERRULED twice over: PD2's stated rationale is that a Task built on a trunk without its base "would re-invent it", and Task 5's actual base (`_fold`, `open_holds`, `append`, `CLASSES` at asf/approvals.py:300 and :340 on origin/main, `job_name` in step_wave.py) has been on the trunk since T-0016, so the guard names the wrong symbol; and it is moot in fact, because T-0019 landed as 6998049 and `def cmd_approvals` now sits at asf/approvals.py:582 on origin/main, so the guard passes. It does not come back in a later round. Second, the branch's one commit was cut before T-0019 landed, so the rebase onto 6998049 collided in asf/approvals.py and tests/test_approvals.py and the worktree came back mid-rebase — that is UPHELD as real work owed, and I made the edit: both sides of both conflicts are purely additive with no redefinition or name collision, so both are kept, with T-0020's `# ---- the tick's raise and the parking (§2.4)` block placed before T-0019's `§2.5` block to keep the file's section headers ascending, the test module docstring naming Task 4 and Task 5, and `CliTest`/`DoctorTest` preceding `TickRaiseTest`. What now holds: T-0020 as committed at 448a676 satisfies all four plan steps within its declared footprint of exactly three files — `raise_holds` returns `{item: (class, level)}` first-in-catalogue-order, one verbatim NEEDS OPERATOR line per open human-now hold oldest first, one groom summary line, `held`/`hold-resolved` written once via the announced/closed markers, and `step_wave.run` parking a held row with no brief and no launch — and its four `TickRaiseTest` methods plus the full 1085-test suite pass. What changes: the loop ends here, the branch is rebased and correct but cannot fast-forward (origin still points at the pre-rebase c6ef2fd), so the factory publishes it; and PD2's guard for Task 5 is spent — no future session should stop on it.
NEEDS OPERATOR: tools/check_conventions.sh could not be run in this sandbox — bash tools/check_conventions.sh

What was disputed is whether T-0021's three sessions failed by writing and pushing nothing, or correctly refused to start. They correctly refused, and I verified the anchor myself rather than taking either side's word: `git show origin/main:asf/tick/step_wave.py | grep -q "raise_holds"` exits 1, `raise_holds` lives only on `origin/worker/T-0020` at c6ef2fd, and `origin/main:asf/approvals.py` carries neither `merge_class` nor `level_of` — so F-0031's PD2 gate is factually unmet and the coders' stop was obedience, not failure. PD2 is upheld exactly as written: no code may be built on this branch until Task 5 is on the trunk, because PD1 makes the wave strictly sequential and Task 5 and Task 6 both write `asf/approvals.py` and `tests/test_approvals.py`, so a Task 6 built on today's main would conflict with T-0020 at harvest. The reading of those three sessions as B-0051 failures is overruled and does not come back in a later round: `pushed: no` marks a failure only when work was done and withheld, and here the plan forbade the work, so there was nothing to push. What now holds is that T-0021 is blocked on a dependency rather than defective, its row closes here, and it is relaunched only after `origin/worker/T-0020` lands on main. What changes is that the loop's real cause is named and is not in T-0021 at all: B-0076 fixed only the reading half — `asf/feeder/rows.py:341` gates on `t.get('after')`, while `asf/record/plan_tasks.py:70-77` mints only `writes` and `stories`, so no plan-minted Task ever carries `after:` and the gate that exists to prevent precisely this stalemate can never fire. That fix is outside T-0021's footprint and is raised as NEEDS OPERATOR above; until it lands, every sequential plan will keep launching Task N before Task N-1.

What was disputed was nothing in the code — there is no round-1 review on this branch (docs/reviews/ holds only 1-b-0005-ruling.md), and no finding was ever written. The single open hold was procedural and factually correct: three sessions produced the complete Task 3 diff in the worktree and each ended without committing it, so origin/worker/T-0018 did not exist and the gate held the branch "unpushed" three times (B-0051), which the record read as a stalemate. That hold is upheld, not overruled — the work genuinely was unpushed — and its exact remedy was to commit the working tree as it stood and push it, which I have done at 6fab061. On the substance I checked every disputed anchor against the checkout myself before landing it: PD2's precondition holds (origin/main:asf/hooks.py names BUILTIN); hook_command/_is_ours gain a product-less form whose `$`-anchored pattern cannot collide with a product rule entry; account_settings_path reads CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR as replacing the runtime's settings directory rather than parenting it, per PD4; install drops the "0 rules declare a hook" early return and narrows the no-repo_dir refusal to the case where a rule actually declares a hook, per PD5; and the two test files carry PD6's new message and byte-level idempotence plus the §3 A2 two-account install case. The gate is green — 1082 tests OK, check_generic clean. What changes is that F-0031's Task 3 is now on a published lane branch for harvest instead of being rewritten a fourth time; no finding was overruled here, because none was ever raised, and the adjudication loop on T-0018 ends with this ruling. Note for the factory: origin/main advanced to 448a676 (T-0020) while this session ran, so the branch is ahead 1 / behind 1 and needs the usual rebase at harvest — I did not merge, rebase or force-push it.

What was disputed is whether T-0026's change is defective, having been held three times on a red gate. It is not. The branch's diff matches plan Task 8354 steps 1-3 exactly: the call to hooks.ensure_git_hooks sits at asf/workers/spawn.py:159-161, after the repo_dir check and above lifecycle.may_launch (:166) and all four worktree paths, so no path reaches git worktree add without the gate (D10); SpawnHookTests covers both reuse paths and all four acceptance tests pass. The gate is nonetheless red, and genuinely so — 1 failure and 5 errors, every one of them tracing to the single line "[step:wave] FAILED module 'asf.hooks' has no attribute 'ensure_git_hooks'". The cause is sequencing, not code: docs/plans/f-0075.md wave order makes T-0026 Task 8354 in wave 3, dependent on 8353 which creates ensure_git_hooks, under the plan's own rule that "nothing below it may start before it lands" — yet asf/hooks.py has no ensure_git_hooks (grep finds it only in T-0026's own commit, the plan and the spec) and asf/redact.py, all of wave 1, does not exist at all. tests/test_sample_product passes clean on origin/main and fails only with this commit, which confirms the attribution without excusing the redness: T-0026 is complete and correct but unlandable, because landing it would break the trunk until its dependency arrives. What now holds: the three corrections are overruled and that finding never returns; the red gate is upheld as a fact but is not a defect of this item, and no fourth correction round is warranted, because no edit within asf/workers/spawn.py or tests/test_workers.py can turn the suite green — the only two that would are implementing another task's footprint, or degrading the call to a getattr fallback that would silently launch sessions into ungated repos and defeat the very guarantee F-0075 exists to give. What changes: T-0026 stops being treated as a failing item and becomes a blocked one, held until Task 8353 lands rather than re-corrected; on that rebase the blanket mock.patch.object(hooks_mod, 'ensure_git_hooks', create=True) in tests/test_workers.py Home.setUp must lose its create=True, which is load-bearing only while the real function is absent and would otherwise mask exactly this class of failure ever after.
NEEDS OPERATOR: T-0026 is blocked on unlanded wave-1 and wave-2 dependencies — land Task 8350 (asf/redact.py) and Task 8353 (hooks.ensure_git_hooks), then rebase task/T-0026; its gate goes green with no change to its diff.

Disputed was whether T-0027 was defective in its own five files, the gate having held it three times. It was not, and the file is the fact in all three places I checked. The sequencing hold recorded on 2026-09-22 is now DISCHARGED BY LANDING, not by correction: `asf/redact.py` arrived on the trunk as T-0022 (73b4a3a), I rebased task/T-0027 onto it with no conflicts, and the branch went green. The three earlier correction rounds remain OVERRULED and do not come back in any later round — none of them could have succeeded, because the two things actually reddening the gate lived outside the lane's footprint. The first was an environment false positive I diagnosed here: `asf/hermetic.py` sets `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0=init.defaultBranch` for every child process, `ENV_SECRET_NAME_RE` matched the KEY in that *name*, and the scanner then hunted the literal string `init.defaultBranch` through the repo's own prose — seven findings, no secrets, and `check_generic: clean` unreachable inside any ASF-run session; unsetting the variable returned rc 0 immediately. That was independently filed and fixed as B-0081 (f3369f9) while I worked, on the same reading, so I did not touch the heuristic — redaction is security, and its edges are not a session's to redraw. The second was `test_the_tracked_pre_push_hook_refuses_an_unpublished_secret`, which errored exactly when the hook did its job: with the push refused, origin's `main` is unborn and `git log main` exits 128 rather than printing nothing, so `_git(check=True)` raised; that is fixed on main as d1c77ef. Of the two anchors the prior ruling said must be verified at the rebase rather than assumed, one is clean — there is exactly one `GitHookTests` class in tests/test_install.py, not a duplicate — and one is UPHELD and still open on the trunk: `tools/check_generic.sh` passes `--names "$PATTERNS_FILE"` for a list `asf.redact` already loads implicitly from the scanned repo, so every finding prints twice, the second copy labelled with the operator's absolute home path rather than `tools/forbidden-names.txt` as D8 requires. `test_a_finding_prints_file_and_line_not_the_word` passes only because `assertIn` does not see the duplicate. I reproduced it against main minutes ago. What changes: T-0027 is settled and needs no further round; the card's acceptance names that third test as `GitHookTests.test_pre_commit_hook_runs_the_suite_without_the_git_hook_environment` when it in fact lives in `PackageTest`, a card-side inaccuracy worth correcting so a future session does not read it as missing; and the duplicate-label defect needs a bug card of its own, since T-0027's lane is closed and I will not mint an id myself (B-0054).
NEEDS OPERATOR: cut and run a bug card for the duplicate finding label in tools/check_generic.sh — `asf new bug "check_generic names the same list twice: every finding prints twice, once with the operator's absolute path"`. The validated fix, inside the old T-0027 footprint: after `cd "$ROOT"`, build the argument conditionally — `NAMES=(); if [ ! -f "$ROOT/tools/forbidden-names.txt" ]; then NAMES+=(--names "$PATTERNS_FILE"); fi` — and call `python3 -m asf.redact --tree ${NAMES+"${NAMES[@]}"} ${EXTRA_FILE:+--names "$EXTRA_FILE"}`. I verified both arms against main: a repo carrying its own list yields the single line `notes.md:2: name (tools/forbidden-names.txt)`, and a repo without one still falls back to the shipped list, so nothing goes unchecked. Worth adding `assertEqual(r.stdout.count('notes.md:2'), 1)` so the duplicate cannot return unseen.
NEEDS OPERATOR: local main (d1c77ef) is four commits ahead of origin/main (e8c992d) and carries all the landed T-0027 and B-0081 work — it is unpublished. Pushing main is never mine; please confirm the factory intends to publish it.

What was disputed was whether `worker/T-0042`'s red gate is a defect in its own diff. It is not, and that reading is overruled for good: I ran the merged pattern set myself and attributed every hit, and ten of the eleven land in asf/evidence/evidence.py, asf/feeder/rows.py, asf/init.py, asf/record/match.py and asf/tick/step_prs.py — files this card's writes: does not carry, whose copies the spec's own table at docs/specs/f-0074.md:284-291 assigns to Tasks 3 and 5, neither of which is on origin/main. The plan's PD2 ordered Task 7 last precisely so those would be gone first; the card was launched out of wave order, so no correction available to this session could have made the gate green, which is why three rounds produced nothing. That finding does not come back in a later round. The eleventh hit was real and was this card's own: T-0042 added `ci-diag-` to tools/forbidden-conventions.txt, which condemned asf/tick/migrate.py:301 — a file PD2's inventory never predicted, and one no purge Task cleans up, so it would have stayed red forever. That finding is upheld. The spec asks for two incompatible things: line 230 lists the pattern, while line 90's non-goal keeps "the hotfix report shape ... the parsers stay as they are", and asf.tick.migrate.hotfix_bug_fields reads the `ci-diag` prefix to choose a severity, not to locate a file — a marker no conventions field in F-0074 carries, so there is no legal fix under this card. What now holds: `ci-diag-` is dropped, with the reason written into the file where the next reader will look; `hotfix-.*-report` stays, because it names a location and reports_dir/report_pattern do carry that. This is the same shape as the plan's own PD3, which overruled a spec bullet on identical grounds. What changes: T-0042's content is complete and correct as of 751db03 and needs no further round, but it must not merge until Tasks 3 and 5 land — its gate is a merge-order fact now, not a defect, and the hardcoded prefix in hotfix_bug_fields survives as a known, recorded gap rather than a silent one.
NEEDS OPERATOR: merge order — hold worker/T-0042 out of main until F-0074's Tasks 3 and 5 land, then re-run `bash tools/check_conventions.sh`; merging it first turns main red, because this card removes the TODO(B-0020) excludes that were masking those ten copies. Recommend requeueing Tasks 3 and 5 ahead of it per the plan's PD2 rather than relaunching this session again.
NEEDS OPERATOR: a Bug card for the residual — `asf.tick.migrate.hotfix_bug_fields` (asf/tick/migrate.py:306) still hardcodes the first product's `ci-diag` report prefix to pick a severity, and F-0074 specifies no conventions field that can carry it. I cannot mint the id (B-0054); run `asf new bug` under F-0074 with that text.

Nothing about T-0037's content was ever actually in dispute — there is no
docs/reviews/1-t-0037.md, no review round produced a finding, and the three holds all read
"unpushed" because the entire diff sat as uncommitted working-tree changes in the worktree
across three sessions. The stalemate was B-0051 repeating, not a disagreement. I checked every
anchor the card cites against the checkout myself: asf/env.py:337-341 on origin/main does set
test_command in exactly the shape the plan quotes, so the fold copies a real precedent;
Conventions already declares ci_workflow, ci_dev_job and deploy_workflow
(asf/conventions.py:149-151), so the fold has somewhere to land; PRODUCT_FIELDS declares
deploy_sha with shape None (asf/env.py:224), so step 2's "not shape-checked today and stays so"
is accurate; and all three named tests exist and pass. The implementation matches plan F-0074
Task 2 line for line, so the unpushed hold is UPHELD with the remedy being to land it — done in
2014f36. Separately I found and UPHELD one defect no round had raised: three of the five new
conventions comments in docs/products.example.yaml named modules that never read the key —
matrix_path was credited to asf.metrics, which contains no reference to it at all (it is read at
asf/evidence/evidence.py:399 and used at :628), and decisions_file/reports_dir were credited to
asf.tick.migrate, which only consumes the text asf.evidence.migrate_sources gathers
(asf/tick/migrate.py:684 reads src.get('sdd_decisions_text')); the real reader is
asf/evidence/evidence.py:839-841. Fixed in 72a02e0; intake_dir's attribution to asf.groom.inbox
was correct (asf/groom/inbox.py:15) and is untouched. Nothing is OVERRULED, because nothing was
ever formally found; for the avoidance of a further round, the fold shape, the CI_FIELDS
addition, the six-value docstring and the three test cases are all ruled correct as they now
stand and do not come back in a later round. What changes: T-0037's work is on origin at
72a02e0, the working tree is clean, and the loop ends here.
NEEDS OPERATOR: two gate legs the sandbox refused — run `bash tools/check_conventions.sh && ./tools/asf plugin check` in /Users/frank/.asf/state/asf/worktrees/coder-t-0037 at 72a02e0; I expect both clean, since asf/env.py matches no forbidden-conventions pattern and the diff touches no plugin file.

The dispute was never a defect in the code — it was three rounds that each produced the correct Task 5 diff and each ended with nine files staged and nothing committed, which is why the hold reads "unpushed" rather than naming a finding; there is no docs/reviews/1-t-0040.md and no docs/specs/t-0040.md, so the branch diff against origin/main was the only document under dispute. I checked every anchor myself. The implementation holds as written: asf/env.py:329 guarantees product.conventions is a Conventions, so branch_for(product, kind, item_id) delegating to .branch() and branch_prefixes(product) delegating to .all_prefixes() are correct, and the deleted default= parameter and WORKER_PREFIX were redundant with Conventions.prefix's per-kind fallback. Two findings are upheld and now fixed on the branch. First, plan decision PD5's claim that dropping 'inbox' from STREAM_FOLDERS breaks no test is wrong: tests/test_backlog.py:231 asserted 'mkdir -p inbox', and I restated it as 'mkdir -p groom' — a folder asf check still requires, keeping B-0005's point that the finding carries a runnable command — plus assertNotIn('inbox/ is missing') to pin the new behaviour; this is a one-file overrun of the declared footprint and is named here rather than left silent. Second, tests/test_inbox_shape.py's make_repo() built inbox/ from STREAM_FOLDERS and stopped creating it, fixed in df8af43 by creating DEFAULT_INTAKE_DIR the way lay_down does. Three findings are overruled and do not come back in any later round: the eleven tests/test_install.py failures are not this diff's, they are asf/workers/runtime.py:102 injecting GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and core.hooksPath into the session so the tests' temp repos inherit the operator's hooks path (git config --show-origin reports "command line:", all 44 pass with those five variables unset, and tests/test_gitfixture.py:21 documents the sandbox doing exactly this); the plan's Gate line naming tests.test_init is stale because tests/test_init.py has never existed in this repo and asf/init.py is covered by tests/test_install.py::InitTest, which is green; and test_sample_product.test_init_creates_the_intake_dir_not_inbox rightly stays skipped, because the second half of its skip reason survives this card — that fixture's asf init takes the adopt branch, so lay_down never runs — and the file belongs to Task 6's writes. What changes: Task 5 of F-0074 is landed and pushed at df8af43 with the full 1277-test suite green and both genericity checks clean, the intake directory and every branch prefix are now read from the product rather than the package, asf check no longer requires an intake directory, and Task 6 inherits the single remaining debt of unskipping the sample's proof.

What was disputed was the gate: T-0047 was held three times on a red suite, with no review file ever written (docs/reviews/1-t-0047.md does not exist in any ref) and so no named finding against the code. The hold is misattributed and is OVERRULED. I exported origin/main — where asf/workers/observe.py does not exist — and ran the four red modules (test_doctor, test_install, test_sample_product, test_gitfixture) against that trunk: 13 failures and 6 errors, a byte-identical list of 19 test names to the branch's. The branch adds no failure and removes none. The cause is environmental and factory-wide: asf launches every worker session with core.hooksPath exported through GIT_CONFIG_* (the deliberate mechanism of docs/specs/f-0076.md D3), and those vars are command-line scope to git, outranking the repo-local core.hooksPath=/dev/null that tests/gitfixture.py:_disable_hooks writes to satisfy B-0073; with them cleared the full suite is green at 1375 tests OK. What now holds is the work as committed at 273b32a: I checked every anchor the card names against the checkout — Observed carries the eight named fields with cwd None, ProcessSource makes one ps axeww call with the default ^(\S*/)?<binary>(\s|$) match and a cycle-guarded ancestor drop, _parse_env takes the five keys with last-occurrence-wins, CommandSource raises ObserveError at read time for a missing sessions_command (D10) rather than at config load, FakeSource returns entries as they stand (D3), source_from_config defaults to process, and read() consumes lifecycle.parse_session, which returns (product, job, stamp) at asf/workers/lifecycle.py:96-107 so the parsed[0]/parsed[1] indexing is correct; ObserveTest and the fake_ps helper exist at tests/test_session_identity.py:246 and :30, and the item's 43 named tests pass. check_generic is clean and the three commented worker_pool keys are in docs/config.example.yaml. What changes because of this: nothing in the branch — no edit was upheld, so there is no commit, and T-0047 is landable as it stands. This overruled finding never comes back in a later round. The one real defect surfaced here — that the suite cannot pass inside an asf worker session because _disable_hooks does not neutralise the inherited GIT_CONFIG_* — belongs to tests/gitfixture.py, outside this item's writes footprint, and is raised as the operator line below rather than fixed here or given an invented id.
NEEDS OPERATOR: the gate is red for every session on this machine, not just T-0047 — tests/gitfixture.py:_disable_hooks writes core.hooksPath=/dev/null to local config, which the session's inherited GIT_CONFIG_* overrides; cut a card (asf new) to make the suite's git calls clear it with the env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT idiom already at asf/workers/githooks.py:43, and until then run the gate as `env -u GIT_CONFIG_COUNT -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_1 -u GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0 -u GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0 python3 tools/run_tests.py`. This likely also explains the T-0037, T-0040 and T-0048 sessions sitting in adjudicate.

What was disputed was never the content of the work but whether T-0048 could be finished at all: three sessions produced the same correct edits and each died inside the >25-minute full suite before committing, so the branch came back empty three times and the record read it as a stalemate. What holds now: the hold is upheld as to fact — the work was real and unpushed, and it is committed and pushed as 49a264e. The blocking fact no round named is upheld as decisive — T-0048's step 2 depends on asf/workers/observe.py from T-9451, which exists on no branch of this repo and is not in this card's writes: footprint, so this card cannot create it and three of its six acceptance tests are unreachable by any amount of further effort; no correction round would have changed that, which is why the loop could not close itself. Overruled, and never to come back in a later round: that T-0048 is wholly blocked — the "counts every product's sessions" half of the item's own title needs only lifecycle.live_all (present at asf/workers/lifecycle.py:178), and it is delivered in 2988ca2 with PoolAcrossProductsTest covering every part reachable without observation, each test checked to fail against the trunk first. Also overruled: that the branch is red — the suite's 13 failures and 29 errors are byte-identical with the branch's files reverted to origin/main, are caused by those tests reading the operator's real ~/.ASF githooks, and are not this card's to fix. What changes: T-0048 carries steps 1, 3, 4, 5 and the registry half of step 2, green and pushed; its remainder is now explicitly T-9451's tail, recorded in from_config's own docstring so the next session finds it at the line rather than in a review file.
NEEDS OPERATOR: T-0048 cannot close as fully done — its remaining acceptance depends on T-9451 (asf/workers/observe.py), which has not landed.
